newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call ends easy, gilts up despite auction.
newsitem.headline: Indian call ends easy, gilts up despite auction.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday easy at 1.0-1.5 percent, unchanged from Thursday's close despite the announcement of a bond auction, dealers said.
They said liquidity with banks was good enough to keep rates down over the next week.
The government on Thursday announced a 30 billion-rupee auction of six-year bonds for July 16.

"Normally there would be fears that a bond auction will drain funds away and squeeze liquidity," said a dealer. "But at the moment, sentiment is good and market players are convinced that liquidity will not be affected significantly."
Dealers said the bond issue will be subscribed in full, given the easy conditions prevailing in the money market.
Prices of government securities rose in active trade, dealers said.

"We are in a bull-run," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Market players are convinced liquidity will remain easy and interest rates low. This has led to good demand for securities despite the bond auction announcement."
"There was good demand for securities particularly with maturities up to 2004," he said.

Among actively traded securities, the 12.59 percent 2004 rose to 101.60 rupees from Thursday's 101.47, the 12.50 percent 2004 to 101.52 from 101.22 and the 13.80 percent 2002 jumped to 106.94 from 106.67, dealers said.
Other stocks which rose included the 13.50 percent 1998 at 103.78 against 103.62 and the 13.12 percent 1999 at 105 against 104.88.
Dealers said treasury bills were also actively traded with July 1998 bills yielding 8.15 percent and April bills 8.0 percent.
